segments.transcript:
Because she was holding a spoon.

Day eleven, I went back to the healer.

He tested the shoulder again.

Better.

Not healed.

He cleared light field work with no overhead load for another week.

I accepted the restriction without arguing.

He looked suspicious.

"What?"

"Nothing."

"You expected an argument."

"Yes."

"I learned."

"From what?"

I thought about it.

Paper.

Bread.

Lorn's jobs.

Tova's measurements.

My father's stupid face at our table.

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
Nessa moving a pot.

The fact that the district had continued operating while I sat in a chair and complained.

"Being useless badly."

The healer smiled.

"You were not useless."

"I know."

That answer surprised me.

Maybe him too.

The shoulder never became good again.

Not completely.

It had already promised that after East Four.

What changed was how I treated the promise.

I stopped carrying certain loads left-handed.

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
Started warming the joint before field reinforcement.

Moved the strap on my tool bag.

Let younger workers take overhead work when the weather made the shoulder angry.

Not every time.

Pride is chronic too.

But more often.

Years later, when I told Ithar about the shoulder, I tried to skip most of that.

I told him the district had started collecting cross-station operator notes around then.

True.

I told him western maintenance policy changed the following winter.

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
Also true.

I told him an A-class Ranker broke a flood gate north of Market and three neighborhoods lost heat for half a day.

Ithar waited.

Dragons are excellent at waiting when they know you are wasting time.

Finally he said,

segments.speaker: ithar
segments.transcript: "You have spent longer describing a flood gate."
